snip.t: In the patient from question 1, blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg with clear lungs and raised jugular venous pressure.
Hypotension, raised jugular venous pressure and muffled heart sounds (Beck's triad) indicate cardiac tamponade after penetrating chest trauma.

Raised jugular venous pressure (JVP): Clear lung fields with elevated JVP and hypotension point directly to right ventricular infarction; elevated JVP with crackles indicates left-sided biventricular failure.
snip.s: Acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction
